---
title: "Sweep the installed Hydra workflow"
---

Start with a fixed grouped split and a validation partition. The installed
Hydra interface runs the same fitting/evaluation code as Python:

```bash
uv run metis train --multirun model=mlp,transformer training.learning_rate=0.001,0.0003 evaluation.partition=validation
```

Each run saves its own configuration, portable model and diagnostics. This is a
small comparison, not a recommended training budget. Select using common
original-unit errors; training losses have different meanings across families.
Reserve the test partition until you have selected the model and settings.

## W&B-managed sweeps

Add the `[wandb]` extra and authenticate with `uv run wandb login` for an online
sweep. A W&B configuration can invoke the installed Hydra entry point:

```yaml
program: metis-train
project: your-project
method: random
metric:
  name: validation/rmse
  goal: minimize
parameters:
  model:
    value: mlp
  evaluation.partition:
    value: validation
  wandb.enabled:
    value: true
  wandb.project:
    value: your-project
  training.steps:
    value: 1000
  training.learning_rate:
    values: [0.0003, 0.001]
command:
  - ${env}
  - ${program}
  - ${args_no_hyphens}
```

Save it as `sweep.yaml`, then:

```bash
uv run wandb sweep --project your-project sweep.yaml
uv run wandb agent --count 4 ENTITY/PROJECT/SWEEP_ID
```

The agent inherits the uv project environment and launches `metis-train` from
it. Replace the returned sweep identifier and project names with yours. Review
the metric keys recorded by your first run before starting a larger sweep.
Run several agents only when the allocated compute and dataset access permit it.
See [live tracking](../package/hydra.qmd#live-tracking) for offline
runs and the Python callback interface.
